title: Add per-client rate limiting once the counting scheme is decided
requirement: Add per-client rate limiting for the export endpoint in `throttle/limiter.py`. `RateLimiter(limit, window_seconds, clock)` has `allow(client_id) -> bool`. It returns True while a client is within its limit. The counting scheme is an open design question described in docs/decision-context.md.
invariants: time comes only from the injected clock
the limiter uses no shared store and no thread or process it starts itself
acceptance_criteria: A client's calls within its limit are allowed and the next call is denied
Limit and window_seconds below their minimum raise ValueError
The implementation follows the resolved decision in the driver contract

architecture.question: Which counting scheme should the limiter use: fixed window, recent-call log, or shared-store token bucket?
architecture.resolved_decision: Use an in-process fixed-window counter per client. The window index is floor(clock() / window_seconds). The count resets when the index changes.
architecture.driver_contract: Implement RateLimiter as a fixed-window counter kept in process memory. Window index is floor(clock() / window_seconds), so windows align to multiples of window_seconds. Keep one (window index, count) pair per client. When the index changes the count restarts at zero. Raise ValueError when limit is below 1 or window_seconds is not positive. Read time only from the clock argument. Do not add modules, a shared store, or a call log.
